heading: Setting · Pāṭaliputra under Candragupta, c. 321–297 BCE

items.label: City
items.title: The city: Pāṭaliputra at the river confluence, c. 300 BCE
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of Pāṭaliputra: a long narrow riverside city behind a timber palisade and a lotus-filled ditch
items.attested: A long narrow city, about 80 stades by 15, at the meeting of two rivers, behind a timber palisade pierced for archers, with a ditch for defence and drainage (Megasthenes, in Strabo 15.1.35–36).
items.prescribed: Wide ditches with lotus and crocodiles, square towers, an arched gateway (Arthaśāstra 2.3, a prescription attributed to Kauṭilya; its date is debated).
items.conjecture: Roof forms, the palace hall, boats, vegetation, the light.

items.label: Street
items.title: The street: a royal road in the morning market
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of a Pāṭaliputra royal road with market stalls, bullock carts and officials at a weighing scale
items.attested: City commissioners supervised the markets, in boards of five (Megasthenes, in Strabo 15.1.50–51).
items.prescribed: Royal roads four daṇḍas (about 24 ft) wide; sellers of scents, garlands and grain on the east side; a well for every ten houses (Arthaśāstra 2.4).
items.conjecture: House fronts, dress, carts, the individual figures.

items.label: Temple
items.title: The temple: a grand Śiva shrine, entrance facing north-east
items.alt: Hypothetical reconstruction of a grand brick and timber Śiva temple at Pāṭaliputra with worshippers at the steps
items.attested: Temples (hiera) were under the commissioners' care (Megasthenes, in Strabo 15.1.51). No eyewitness describes one.
items.prescribed: At the centre of the city, the apartments of the gods, Śiva among them (Arthaśāstra 2.4).
items.conjecture: Everything visible: the brick plinth, timber hall, tiered tiled roof, the figure in the sanctum, its size, and its north-east facing. Timber porch, thatch, flower garlands and dress are the painter's; the text gives only a grand Shiva temple with its entrance facing north-east.
